name: Nasturtium

schedule.notes: Doesn't transplant well — taproot. Soak seeds 12 hours first.
Pick flowers daily; pick leaves at any size. Green seed pods can be pickled as 'poor man's capers'.

harvest.cues: Flowers fully open, bright orange/yellow/red. Leaves any size, round and lily-pad-like.
harvest.storageNotes: Flowers wilt within hours — eat the same day. Pickled seed pods keep months.

varieties.name: Alaska
varieties.notes: White-marbled leaves, bushy 12 in. Compact for borders.

varieties.name: Empress of India
varieties.notes: Deep red flowers against blue-green leaves. Classic heirloom.

varieties.name: Trailing Jewel Mix
varieties.notes: Vining to 6 ft. Mixed colors. Great over fences and edges.

notes: Both leaves and flowers are edible — peppery, like a mild radish. Used as a trap crop: aphids prefer nasturtiums to your vegetables. Self-seeds in zone 7+; treat as annual elsewhere.
